cards.f: How long is each IGCSE English First Language (0500) paper, and how many marks?
cards.b: 2 hours, 80 marks. Each paper is worth 50% of the grade.
Reading, with some marks for writing. Three texts (A, B, C) in a reading booklet insert.
Writing, with some marks for reading in Section A. Directed writing then composition.

cards.f: Paper 1 summary: word limit and form?
cards.b: No more than 120 words, in continuous prose. Marked 10 reading + 5 writing = 15.

cards.f: Which text is Q1 summary based on, and which text is Q2 and Q3 based on?
cards.b: Summary: Text B. Q2 and Q3: Text C. Q1 short answers use Text A.

cards.f: Paper 1 Q3 (extended response): marks, length and split?
cards.b: 25 marks: 15 reading + 10 writing. 250-350 words in a set form such as letter, speech or article.

cards.f: Paper 2 Section A: marks, length and split?
cards.b: 40 marks: 15 reading + 25 writing. 250-350 words, argumentative or discursive, using two texts.

cards.f: Paper 2 Section B: what choice do you get, and marks?
cards.b: One of four titles: two descriptive, two narrative. 40 marks: 16 content and structure + 24 style and accuracy. 350-450 words.

cards.f: What do R1 and R2 test?
cards.b: R1: explicit meanings (what is stated). R2: implicit meanings and attitudes (what is implied).
Understanding how writers achieve effects and influence readers (the writer's effect question).
By levels: the examiner reads the whole answer and picks the best-fit level, then a mark within it.
Point-based: one mark per correct idea. Own-words questions give no mark for copied key words.

cards.f: Why is writing 600 words for a 350-450 word composition risky?
cards.b: Loose structure, loss of control, more errors (W5) and less time to check. Length is guidance, not a target.
Spending too long on Q1 and rushing Q3, which is worth 25 marks.

short.q: State the five question types on Paper 1 in order (Q1 short answers, Q1 summary, ...). [3]
short.model: Q1 short answers on Text A, Q1 summary on Text B, Q2 short answers on Text C, Q2 writer's effect on Text C, Q3 extended response on Text C.
points: Q1 short answers (Text A) and summary (Text B)
Q2 short answers and writer's effect (Text C)

short.q: How are the 40 marks split in Paper 2 Section A, and what is the task? [3]
short.model: 15 marks for reading and 25 for writing. You write an argumentative or discursive piece evaluating the ideas in two texts.

short.q: Explain the difference between R1 and R2, with an example. [2]
short.model: R1 is explicit: the text says there was no electricity. R2 is implicit: children did homework by candlelight, so you infer life was hard.

short.q: A student writes a summary as bullet points. Why does this lose marks? [2]
short.model: The summary must be continuous prose. Note form or lists lower the writing mark because ideas are not organised or linked.

short.q: Why does a student's 600-word composition risk a low style and accuracy mark? [3]
short.model: Longer answers often lose control and contain more errors, and structure becomes loose, and less time is left for checking.
